thread:
joel: quick thread  Product asked for a safer deprec window. idea: per-tenant deprecation escrow that keeps a short-lived compatibility fallback for ‘high-risk’ customers while telemetry collects impact signals. thoughts?

tasha: can you expand  escrow = automatic temporary grace for flagged tenants? how is it different from our current grace toggles?

joel: two differences: 1) escrow is ephemeral and tied to measured customer impact (errors, latency, user-visible regressions). It auto-expires when signals are clean. 2) escrow is per-tenant and per-route and appears in console as an "Escrow period" with start/estimated end. Not a manual unlimited opt-out.

ravi: interesting. how do we decide who is "high-risk"? product proposed rule: customers with >1k daily active tokens or customers who previously filed a compatibility complaint. but better to base on a risk_score computed from usage patterns + SDK age.

marta: telemetry-wise we need: 1) a signal feed of `compat.error_rate`, `semantic-drift-regressions`, `client-sdk-age` and 2) an escrow controller that consumes signals and exits escrow when metrics under thresholds for N windows.

tasha: console UX: show escrow banner: "Escrow active: we are temporarily preserving v1 compatibility for you while monitoring. This is a short-lived safety measure." Also include CTA to request extension (audit log required).

joel: ops implications: during escrow we 1) route by served-compatibility (prefer v1 if fallback seen), 2) apply a soft quota cap so experiments don't consume more than steady-state, and 3) emit escrow-specific telemetry tags. We must avoid letting escrow be abused to bypass billing/limits.

ravi: on quotas: we should track two counters: `quota.units.actual` (what served) and `quota.units.escrow_protected` (units protected by escrow). Escrow protects from immediate hard decomm but still counts for capacity and billing. That keeps invoices accurate while giving devs time to fix issues.

marta: agree. we will add `escrow_id` to every telemetry event during the window so finance and ops can filter. Also emit `escrow.exited` and `escrow.extended_request` events.

tasha: policy for extension requests: tenant admins can request +1x 24h extension via console but it creates an audit entry and requires SRE review for high-traffic tenants. auto-extensions allowed only for tiny tenants (<100DAU).

ravi: algorithm sketch (pseudocode):
```
if tenant.risk_score > R && compat.error_rate > E for 3/5 windows:
  create_escrow(tenant, route, ttl=24h, escrow_id=uuid())
else: no action
```
Escrow controller will re-evaluate every 10m and close early if error_rate < E_low for 6 consecutive windows.

joel: security/abuse: escrow must not alter billing. escrow protects the tenant from abrupt feature removal, not from fees. Console copy should be explicit.

marta: telemetry storage: tag events with `escrow_id` and `escrow_phase` (entering, monitoring, exiting). We also store a small sample of request/response pairs (opt-in) for up to 7 days to debug regressions. Need legal sign-off for payload retention.

tasha: UI: small timeline in route details: Escrow start, ETA, current metric status (error_rate, seqlen drift), and a one-click request extension button (admins only). Default ETA computed from rolling average time-to-stabilize in historical similar rollouts.

ravi: implementation tasks: escrow-controller service (stateless worker + persistent record), routing-affinity adjustments during escrow, telemetry tag plumbing, console components, and audit logging. Must be feature-flagged.

joel: developer notes: routing-affinity during escrow should prefer served variant but not hard-pin; allow controlled fallbacks with exponential backoff to reduce oscillation. Also, add a per-tenant escrow cap so we don't keep too many long-lived escrows.

marta: metrics to add: `escrow.active_count`, `escrow.avg_duration`, `escrow.fix_rate` (percent that self-resolve), and `escrow.resource_overlap` (percent of escrowed units against variant capacity).

tasha: rollout plan: internal alpha (internal tenants) -> invite-only partners -> opt-in beta. Console flag default OFF for public.

ops-bot: escrow-controller feature flagged deploy scheduled to canary at 2024-12-18T22:00:00Z.

ravi: open question: should escrow be visible in public API (headers, route metadata) or console-only? I lean console-only to avoid client-side logic changes.

joel: agree console-only. keep server-side telemetry and routing changes internal. If partners want API hooks we can add later with strict signing.

marta: I'll draft RFC with signal thresholds and telemetry schema and loop in legal/finance for retention and export requirements.

tasha: thanks. I'll mock the console banner copy and extension flow. We'll reconvene after RFC draft.
